subject: Hosted API pricing qualification: expected monthly token volume + peak TPS
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@fintechco.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com, alex_martinez@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 08 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API pricing qualification: expected monthly token volume + peak TPS

Hi Alicia — great to meet on the call today. Quick recap and a couple of asks so our pricing/solutions team can model this correctly: 

Call recap (high level):
- Primary use case: personalized customer support summaries + follow-up suggestions (near real-time).
- Expected production start: Q3 2026 pilot, ramp to full production over 3–6 months.
- Latency requirement: sub-300ms for 95th pct on single-request generation (short prompts ~200 tokens).

What we need to price hosted API appropriately:
1) Estimated monthly token volume (preferred: avg/month and expected peak month). If you can give a breakdown of prompt vs. completion tokens that helps.
2) Peak sustained TPS (transactions per second) during business hours and absolute burst TPS.
3) Target $/1M tokens (if you have an internal target or budget range we should align to).
4) Any constraints on data residency or contract timeline that would affect price (SLA, PII handling).

If easier, I attached a quick worksheet (pricing_estimate_v1.xlsx) you can fill with approximate numbers — we can iterate. Based on similar pilots, a typical starting point is 50M–200M tokens/month with peak TPS in the 10–40 TPS range; but we'll tailor to your traffic patterns.

Next steps: if you can reply with the items above, I’ll put together a hosted pricing estimate and run it by our finance team for any volume discounts.

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0123

From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@fintechco.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com, alex_martinez@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 08 Jun 2026 18:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing qualification: expected monthly token volume + peak TPS

Hi Ben — thanks for the recap and the worksheet, helpful. Preliminary numbers from our product team: 

- Expected avg monthly token volume (pilot): ~30M tokens/month (prompt ~8M, completion ~22M)
- Expected avg monthly tokens (prod ramp): 180M tokens/month (prompt ~36M, completion ~144M)
- Peak month (marketing + feature launch): estimate ~300M tokens
- Peak sustained TPS (business hours): ~25 TPS; absolute burst up to ~80 TPS for short windows (a few minutes)
- Target $/1M tokens: our internal budget target is in the $18–$25 per 1M tokens range for hosted APIs (we benchmarked a few vendors)

Notes: We care about predictable unit economics (so pricing with clear overage buckets helps) and also model-based fallbacks if capacity is constrained. No special data residency for the pilot; will circle back if enterprise requirements change.

Happy to hop on a short call with Alex to walk through request patterns if helpful.

—Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Head of Product, FintechCo
alicia.gomez@fintechco.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@fintechco.com>, procurement@fintechco.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com, alex_martinez@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 09 Jun 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing qualification: expected monthly token volume + peak TPS

Thanks Alicia — this is exactly what we needed. A couple follow-ups/clarifications before I build the formal estimate: 

- For the prod ramp numbers, is the 180M tokens/month expected at steady-state or mid-ramp average? (i.e., should we model a linear ramp 3–6 months to reach 180M, or treat 180M as the steady-state for pricing tiers?)
- For peak burst behavior (80 TPS), can you share whether those bursts are evenly distributed across the day or concentrated to specific hours/events? This impacts our autoscaling and cost modeling.
- Do you expect a high ratio of streaming responses or single-shot completions? Streaming tends to shift cost and latency characteristics.

I'll draft two pricing scenarios and attach them: (A) pilot + conservative ramp (tiered hosted pricing with a modest commit) and (B) aggressive ramp (better volume discounts + reserved baseline). Also attaching our vendor onboarding packet for procurement (vendor_onboarding_packet.pdf) — if procurement wants an official quote, please loop them in and we’ll produce a DocuSign-ready proposal.

Would you and procurement be available Thursday 10:00am PT for a 30min price review? I can have Alex join to go over TPS/architecture implications.

Best,
Ben

From: procurement@fintechco.com <procurement@fintechco.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@fintechco.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 09 Jun 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing qualification: expected monthly token volume + peak TPS

Hi Ben — procurement here. We reviewed the onboarding packet and Alicia's numbers. Please provide: 

1) A formal pricing estimate (PDF) showing line items for pilot (30M/mo), ramp (180M/mo), and peak (300M/mo) including $/1M assumptions, any committed discounts, and overage terms.
2) Expected SLA (latency targets and uptime) for hosted API and any credits for missed SLOs.
3) Vendor onboarding details: legal entity information, W-9, and primary account manager contact.

We prefer the pricing to include a $/1M tokens summary (so our finance team can easily compare). Targeting to complete vendor selection by 2026-06-18. 

Thanks — Procurement
procurement@fintechco.com
